Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from isolated indigenous communities, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31.

Eighth Part
Protection of Children Who Require Special Protection

Article 39
(1) Special Protection for Children from isolated indigenous communities as referred to in Article 36 letter c shall be carried out through the provision of facilities and infrastructure so that they can enjoy their own culture, acknowledge and practice their own religious teachings, and use their own language.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from obstructing Children as referred to in paragraph (1) from enjoying their own culture, acknowledging and practicing their own religious teachings, and using their own language, without disregarding access to the development of society and culture.

Article 42
(1) Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f is carried out through efforts of supervision, protection, prevention, care, rehabilitation and reintegration by the Regional Government and the Community.
(2) To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Courts, the Community, NGOs and Social Organizations take steps in the form of:
 a. conducting outreach/socialization and/or campaigns regarding the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
 b. carrying out cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with statutory regulations.
(3) Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking is implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government institutions or the Community.
(4) Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking has the right to obtain care and rehabilitation, both physical and psychological, and reintegration in the family environment as well as in the Community.

Article 44
(1) Special Protection for Children with special needs as referred to in Article 36 letter h shall be carried out through efforts to:
a. treat Children humanely in accordance with the dignity and Rights of the Child;
b. fulfill special needs; and
c. provide equal treatment with other Children in order to achieve social integration as fully as possible and individual development.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from treating Children with special needs in a discriminatory manner, by disregarding their views, including labeling and equal treatment in education for Children with special needs.

Article 45
(1) Special Protection for Children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, care and rehabilitation.
(2) Every person and/or any party who places or allows, and is also prohibited from involving or ordering the involvement of, a Child in situations of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSES
Article 46
(1) Women and Child victims of Violence who require continuous handling have the right to stay in a safe house.
(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored.
(3) The organization and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women and Child Empowerment.
(4) Further provisions regarding the organization of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Fifth Part
Protection of Children Under Five Years of Age

Article 26
(1) Placement of a Child in a temporary shelter as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on identification results it is known that:
a. the safety of the Child is threatened;
b. the Child does not have a family/caregiver or guardian; and
c. the Child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the Community.
-1- (2) Placement as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be carried out for a certain period of time while the Child receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is assessed to have the readiness to care for and protect the Child. (1) Rescue action as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b shall be carried out if, based on the results of identification, it is known that the safety of the Child is threatened.

Article 40
(1) Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d is carried out through:
a. prevention of the exploitation of Children under supervision/monitoring who are utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;
b. dissemination and/or socialization of laws and regulations related to the Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, trade unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.

Article 43
(1) Every Child who is a victim of physical and/or psychological Violence as referred to in Article 36 letter g shall receive rehabilitation services, both physical and psychosocial.
(2) Forms of protection for Child victims of acts of Violence include basic social services, education, religious guidance, health services, psychological counseling and/or psychotherapy, legal assistance, recreational and educational activities, and empowerment of parents of Child victims of acts of violence.

Article 41
(1) Special Protection for Children who are victims of narcotics abuse including aromatic glue and the like that can cause hallucinatory effects and the like as referred to in Article 36 letter e, and involved in the use, production and distribution thereof, shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
